title: Thames — ISIS-II 8080/8085 command-line tool runner
reason: Approved original CLI-runner discovery. Mark Ogden’s maintained Thames source explicitly derives from John Elliott’s Thames 0.1.1. Elliott’s official page identifies an ISIS-II runner for the tools used to build CP/M3, and the maintained loader/interpreter confirm direct original-binary execution. Count the original tarball and enhanced fork as one lineage under ogdenpm/thames-src. CP/M3 is the build product of example guest tools, not the OS API being emulated. Canonical root was absent from the fresh 1702-project baseline at ac4ea751fcdb273322cfdac18cd679b83f03a90f and the prior deduplication index. Inspected default-branch head: dd545328888b6e989c5975053372d97a36dc336f. Modern tooling executes linked ISIS-II Intel OMF images, often without file extensions. isis_load accepts module/start/data/end records, loads bytes and rejects unresolved relocation/external/library records. main creates synthetic MDS BIOS/ISIS trap stubs in RAM, loads the argv-selected tool and enters the interpreter. ISIS OPEN/CLOSE/READ/WRITE/SEEK/LOAD translate to host files through device mapping; the path needs original tools/support files but no original boot ROM or booted ISIS OS. John Elliott origin and Mark Ogden enhancements remain one Thames family. The interpreter has GPL-2.0-or-later headers and COPYING is GPLv2; several ISIS/loader files have GNU Library GPL v2-or-later notices, so preserve mixed component terms. Original Intel tools are separately licensed. Documentation recommends newer native-C ports for several tools; those execute recompiled source and must not be conflated with Thames running originals. The previous documentation-only hold is superseded by this pinned source audit. Wider author, dependency and fork-graph coverage remains partial.

reason: Native Amstrad CPC platform/action game by Samuel Bolanowski and Atharuddin Syed, built with CPCtelera and a duck/bubble-themed character and enemy set.

title: Mitosis
reason: Ataxx-style RISC OS desktop board game in RiscLua, including full board/rules classes and native Toolbox wrapper integration. Source and a bundled standalone runtime application are present.

title: Pilot VT100 — native Palm OS serial terminal
reason: Preserved 1990s Pilot VT100 application source and later Palm OS 4 SDK compatibility patch, implementing serial terminal I/O, escape parser, screen handling and configurable keys.

title: HalfWorm — native OS/2 source continuation
reason: Jan M. Danielsson’s 1997 two-player worm combat game restored for OpenWatcom with native DIVE graphics, MMPM/2 audio and configurable keyboard/joystick input. Its substantial game-thread code implements worms, missiles, apple powerups and round results.

title: Last Resort Neo
reason: Native NGPC fan reimagining of SNK’s Last Resort with two ships, five stages, orbital option-pod control, charged wave cannon, multiple pod weapons and monochrome mode. main.c has stage terrain installation, pod movement/fire and independent game progression.

title: LitesOut — native OS/2 source continuation
reason: Herbert Bushong’s 1996–1997 OS/2 Lights Out puzzle continued as a plain-C 32-bit Presentation Manager rewrite of its preserved Borland OWL source. The 6×8 board has two-state and three-state modes, scoring and persistent settings.

title: Othello for OS/2 — native OS/2 source continuation
reason: Peter Wansch’s 1994 native Reversi game continued in OpenWatcom with preserved ICC sources. Its independent engine implements legal-move detection, disc flipping, positional evaluation and recursive multi-level computer search.

title: Super Puzzle Fighter II Turbo: SNK vs CAPCOM — NGPC homebrew
reason: Native puzzle-fighter proof of concept with falling gem pairs, rotations, gravity, crashes, rectangular power gems, chain damage, CPU garbage attacks, story/endless modes and unlocks. src/game.c contains actual grid/phase resolution and difficulty tables; field.c renders through NGPC tile hardware.

title: Rutgers Pascal — PDP-10 compiler and runtime sources
reason: Historical Rutgers Pascal compiler sources recovered from University of Utah, including Pascal compiler implementation, MACRO-10 runtime/debugger/I/O modules, command files and detailed manuals.

title: Synthwave — AmigaOS game framework
reason: Robin Southern’s native AmigaOS 3.x C game framework supplies event, time, memory, window, input and planar/chunky framebuffer implementations, including a 68000-family chunky-to-planar assembly component. This is a reusable native framework, not an emulator wrapper.

title: S1C88 C Tools for Pokémon Mini
reason: Cross-platform installation/build integration for the EPSON/TASKING S1C88 compiler, including Pokémon Mini headers, locator configuration, startup assembly and an executable hello-world source example. This is an SDK integration project, not a reconstruction of the proprietary compiler.

title: Wake on LAN for Windows 3.1
reason: Preserved Pascal source of Depicus’s Windows 3.1 Wake-on-LAN utility, with VCL application/forms and a component implementing socket-based magic-packet transmission.

title: Avalanche — Amiga ReAction archive manager
reason: Native ReAction GUI for xadmaster, xfdmaster and Deark with tabbed archive browsing/extraction, LhA/Zip modification, optional virus scanning, disk images and ARexx integration.

title: Batman — Acorn Archimedes ARM port prototype
reason: An independently written ARM implementation of the Amiga Batman game with converted graphics, scrolling tile maps, compiled sprites, player movement/collision tests and projectile updates. This is a partial game port, not the already tracked MarkyTurtle Amiga source reconstruction.

title: CP/67 CMS — tape-recovered operating-system sources
reason: Recovered original CMS assembler source, macro definitions and assembly listings from old CP/67-format tapes. Recovery used VM/370 and z/VM conversion before ASCII extraction. The repository name mentions CP/67; inspected payload is specifically CMS, with source headers dated 1973 as well as older material, not a verified complete CP kernel.

title: HEX2TAPE_LGP30 — Intel HEX to native tape converter
reason: Companion Python tool converts sparse Intel HEX LGP-30 binaries into v-formatted LGP-30 paper-tape text, preserving start address in Stop and Transfer records. Implementation groups segments into chunks, writes tape headers and encodes the machine’s nonstandard hexadecimal alphabet.

title: SIM_LGP30 — Python machine simulator and debugger
reason: Neil Higgins’s reusable Python LGP-30 simulator models instructions, drum memory, Flexowriter input/output, paper-tape and Intel HEX loading, with interactive debugging controls and recovered program examples. Its stated goal is a hackable simulator suited to future MicroPython use rather than cycle accuracy.

title: XASM_LGP30 — symbolic Python cross-assembler
reason: Neil Higgins’s two-pass LGP-30 cross-assembler provides structural validation, symbols and expressions, directives, formatted listings and Intel HEX binary output. Modernized syntax intentionally differs from the historical native assemblers.

title: GameX-Gels — native Amiga graphics library
reason: ANSI C AmigaOS game-development library implementing screens, Copper synchronization, IFF loading, icons and graphics.library-compatible BOB/VSprites with custom accelerated blitter/mask operations. Substantial reusable graphics subsystem rather than the author's skeletal Blaster game.

title: libpressf — portable Fairchild F8 emulation library
reason: Reusable C89 emulation library for Fairchild F8-family systems, including Channel F. Models the CPU instruction/ROMC machinery and memory, display, beeper, controllers and auxiliary devices; shared by multiple distinct platform frontends.

title: Nuclear Reaction — C64 implementation
reason: Native Commodore 64 implementation based on Amiga Nuclear Reaction. C/6502 assembly provides atom-placement chain reactions, two-player turns, winner detection, AI search, PETSCII rendering, SID sound and hardware input. Substantial independent game implementation.

title: OVER REV racing engine template — native NGPC road renderer
reason: A standalone source template extracted from the original OVER REV Neo Geo Pocket Color racer. Promote only the reusable engine/sample in the checked-in ZIP: the full game is distributed as binaries and explicitly has not had its complete source published.

title: Pascal-Monitor — BESM-6 compiler reconstruction and C++ conversion
reason: Reconstructs the Pascal compiler included in the Dubna monitor from a recovered object module. Includes disassembly, annotated recovery material, Pascal auxiliaries and a direct C++ translation that emits big-endian BESM-6 object modules.

title: Star Fighter — DIV Games Studio 2 DOS game
reason: Original 2020 game-jam pseudo-3D space shoot-em-up using vanilla DOS DIV Games Studio 2 and mode-7-style presentation. PRG game source and custom Watcom C++ DLL modules are included.

title: Xpw — original X11 widget library
reason: Cornwell's 1990s X Toolkit widget set developed alongside XMS mail, addressing Athena widget limitations through cascaded menus, selection controls, cached 3D drawing and an extensible widget library.

title: arcimage
reason: Restored 1997-2000 Turbo Pascal-era PC utility that reads and writes physical Archimedes floppy sectors into emulator-compatible disk images, including later F-format improvements.

title: Bomb Jack Revisited — VIC-20 native game
reason: Author ops’s 1985 VIC-20 game revisited in 2018, with BASIC game administration and interrupt-driven assembly movement/music. Distinct VIC-20 implementation of the arcade theme.

title: DOS development template with serial GDB stub
reason: Turnkey native DOS game/demo development environment integrating DJGPP, CMake/Ninja, VS Code and DOSBox-X with a substantive custom remote GDB serial debugging stub.

title: FiZZ — VIC-20 platform puzzle game
reason: Native VIC-20 FiZZ platform-puzzle implementation in Turbo Rascal, with modular object physics, control, lasers/floater/fontaine components and JSON level data.

title: Gateway
reason: Native Classic Toolbox PowerPC Mac OS 9 and Win32 gateway/proxy application that supplies modern TLS, mail splicing, Wayback forwarding and tunnels to vintage clients.

title: GB-EMU — reusable Game Boy emulator for 3DS
reason: Reusable C++ Game Boy emulator targeting Nintendo 3DS. Pinned implementation contains SM83 operand/opcode execution, PPU scanline rendering, cartridge memory banking, APU, timer, joypad, ROM browsing and a platform/core separation. It loads general Game Boy ROMs rather than wrapping one game.

title: Bounce Tales
reason: Readable Java reconstruction with extracted-resource tooling and Jademula Windows layer. Explicitly targets behaviour rather than identical bytecode.

title: Kaypro D.COM
reason: Commented NASM reconstruction of a 3552-byte directory utility with DOS/BIOS simulation fixtures. Kaypro provenance is described as believed, not certain.

title: Tool Blocks
reason: Original MSX BASIC homebrew with editable ASCII source and packaged ROM version. Source publication, not a commercial-game decompilation.

title: CapriceRPI — Raspberry Pi CPC emulator port
reason: Substantive Caprice32 4.1.0 adaptation with joystick-driven virtual keyboard, four-controller/ToTo support, autorun, snapshots and Pi-specific display handling. Includes emulator core and source build files rather than only a packaged binary.

title: The Last Pumpkin — C64 TRSE game
reason: Halloween-themed C64 game with obstacle entities, sprites, collision logic and joystick/paddle input. Main TRSE source and included obstacle module are substantial, not only images or a binary release.

title: NDEC — DOS cryptor analysis and Go reconstruction
reason: Documents a small DOS COM cryptor’s unpacked algorithm and supplies matching high-level encryption/decryption code and tests.

title: on-the-spectrum — traceable Rust Spectrum emulator
reason: Shared Z80 decoder feeds interpreter/disassembler; explicit machine-cycle primitives expose per-T-state bus traces. Bevy frontend and headless testing paths exist.

title: disASM — relocatable Spectrum disassembler
reason: Compact native Z80 disassembler with internal stack, IX/IY undocumented-register decoding and relocation support.

title: civ-extract — Civilization graphics and fonts
reason: Decodes MicroProse PIC/PAL graphics, sprite sheets and FONTS.CV, with atlas and JSON-index output. Inspected variable-width LZW implementation and framing.

title: Oh Mummy Resurrected — Amstrad Plus remake
reason: Substantial native Oh Mummy adaptation with keyboard scanning, sound jump tables, object maps and Plus sprite support.

title: Gradient Blaster — retro palette and Copper exporter
reason: Interactive gradient interpolation/dithering tool exports palette tables, big-endian binary and Amiga Copper lists, with ST/STE/Falcon format encoders.

title: Device Streams — modernized Amiga disk imaging
reason: RDB information and device-to-stream/stream-to-device utilities with modernized 64-bit offsets, TD64/NSD support and overflow safeguards.

title: BBC MOS 1.20 — BeebAsm reconstruction and extensions
reason: Converts Toby Nelson’s annotated ACME MOS disassembly to BeebAsm and supplies original/optimized conditional builds with a revised line editor.

title: Mystery House — archaeological analysis scripts
reason: Research scripts decode Mystery House dictionaries, messages, objects, rooms and graphics data, with captured outputs. Accompanies the authors' 2019 archaeological study.

title: Makepool/colour-mapper
reason: Only a 27-byte README saying Amiga tool is present. No implementation or substantive documented release is available to qualify.

title: ahx2txt — Amiga AHX module inspection
reason: Decodes AHX headers, subsongs, positions, tracks and instruments into readable text.

title: Aseprite ILBM I/O — legacy import/export script
reason: Aseprite Lua script imports/exports basic ILBM/LBM with explicitly limited special-mode and cycling support.

title: HunkFile — Rust reader and writer
reason: Library exposes block iteration, structured file representation and writing for Amiga executable/object/library data with configurable parsing.

title: CPC Sprite Tool — Svelte pixel editor
reason: Browser 8x8 four-color editor packs four pixels into CPC-style bytes and exports assembly data directives.

title: Autodoc DataType — native API documentation rendering
reason: Datatype parses Autodoc sections and marker decorations and formats documentation using native class methods.

title: Scrolling BASIC Editor — original 1987 C64 source
reason: Author-published original source for the scrolling editor distributed in COMPUTE! Gazette January 1988, including keyboard and IRQ-vector integration.

title: jartificer/IFFtoWAV
reason: Inspected batch script delegates conversion to SoX, selecting 8SVX versus fixed-rate raw fallback via a FORM text search and preserving directory layout. Useful collection-specific automation, but no independent codec or substantial analysis implementation warrants another catalogue entry.

title: Fast AY Player — CPC replay and YM cruncher
reason: Host YM cruncher and native relocatable replay code target low, song-dependent fixed playback cost.

title: MAX 4.0 — partial Korean DOS conversation-engine recovery
reason: Reimplements keyword/response-group selection and extracts legacy response data, with documented unresolved Korean encoding and original far-pointer table analysis.

title: KsmBl/civ1-recompiled
reason: Static x86-to-C lifting retains runtime CPU, dispatch and interpreter modules. Native hook features do not establish whole-game high-level reconstruction; keep game-specific emulation audit separate from richardpenman/civ1.

title: retrocoils/solar-winds-js
reason: Inspected tree has only README declaration, without committed reconstruction implementation. Preserve lead until actual source appears.

title: slippyex/OSME
reason: Tree contains an emu68-based music engine and bundled playback sources; not established as reconstruction of a requested historical game/application. Root README could not be decoded via blob fetch, so no stronger claim is made.

title: Scorched Earth — JavaScript engine recovery
reason: Native JavaScript artillery systems backed by original executable addresses, FPU decoding and independent execution probes; offline Python x86 oracle is separate from browser gameplay.

title: The Reconstruction of ZZT — Turbo Pascal source
reason: Reconstructs ZZT 3.2 engine, editor, scripting runtime and data builder from the lost-source release.

title: QuickBASIC QLB — library runtime reconstruction
reason: Reverse-engineers QuickBASIC 4.0/4.5 quick-library container and dispatcher, with annotated Microsoft runtime listing, native loader and working library examples.

title: ThaiD 2.3.88 — DOS Thai driver analysis
reason: Annotated Thai-language investigation maps TSR interrupts, keyboard/printer paths, three-band glyph rendering, KU/TIS codes and configuration structures.

title: Ultima IV — TypeScript/Tauri reconstruction
reason: Address-linked combat, world, town, dungeon and intro logic recovered from AVATAR/TITLE with native TypeScript state; original executable is read as data, not executed.

title: igorrehem/yfm-native
reason: Targets PlayStation Forbidden Memories SLUS-01411, not the requested DOS/Amiga/ST/CPC platforms. Do not mistake Windows output platform for original DOS provenance.

title: missingno7/overkill_port
reason: Contains genuine recovered-domain work, but reviewed status explicitly retains generated block dispatchers and differential coverage debt. Requires a focused current architecture audit before calling the full game a VM-less high-level source port.

title: PCBoard PPL/PPE — Rust runtime and language reconstruction
reason: PCBoard script compiler/decompiler, executable parser and console runtime with actual PPE-command evaluator. Language bytecode VM is not emulation of DOS CPU instructions.

title: BtechPort — BattleTech recreation and construction kit
reason: Independent C11 rules, original-data extraction and configurable construction kit, derived from executable observations and UnBattletech research.

title: zxtap-to-wav — Go Spectrum tape encoder
reason: Converts TAP blocks to audio pilot, synchronization and data pulses with adjustable output rate, gain and inter-block gaps; native and WASM entry points.

title: py6502 — scriptable assembler and simulator
reason: Python APIs assemble code, share object maps/symbols with disassembly and simulation, and enable host-programmed instrumentation instead of an assembler macro language.

title: TIImageTool — TI99 disk and filesystem workbench
reason: Manages TI floppy/hard-disk image layouts, allocation and files, with BASIC and GPL/native-code analysis components.

title: Cosmo — Cosmore-derived portable C continuation
reason: Builds Scott Smitelli’s recovered Cosmore source against portable DOS service and EGA interfaces, retaining game logic while adapting rendering/audio.

title: SCUMM games — organized script decompilation archive
reason: Organizes recovered room/global scripts from Lucasfilm and Humongous titles using descumm and later NUTcracker.

title: itpick/warlords2-decompile
reason: README identifies PowerPC Mac reconstruction and InfiniteMac comparisons; not DOS Warlords II despite discovery-list grouping.

title: Dungeon Plunder
reason: Real native vintage-machine game family, but source review only found the Colour Maximite 2 BASIC prototype. Vintage ports are represented by screenshots, some binaries, or commercial download links; no Z80 implementation/build source was present in the reviewed recursive tree. Exclude from the source-verified batch rather than overstate published port source. No project is added by this decision. No build or runtime verification was performed.

title: retrostack/trs-80-model-i-jap20-e1
reason: KiCAD hardware replica, outside software-focused clean batch. README explicitly warns unconfirmed working state and original trace defects/jumper requirements. No project is added by this decision. No build or runtime verification was performed.

title: digarok/TransWarpGS-ROM
reason: Complete 65816 ROM disassembly with Merlin32 reassembly and 100% parity.

title: david-schmidt/AII2048
reason: README explicitly bases the Apple II/III port on chesterbr/2048-2600, already catalogued as 2048-atari-2600. Preserve the port as a same-engine lineage lead rather than silently adding another independent 2048 implementation. Jeremy Rand’s C implementation is separately authored.

title: Lode Runner: earlier Simon Hung implementation
reason: The README directs readers to Total Recall as the new version. Preserve one lineage and promote the successor instead of counting the old JavaScript release or its many forks separately.

title: metatermin8r/pathways-into-darkness-unity
reason: Source implements level geometry, doors, transitions and partial player state, so README claims of no functionality are stale. Later companion notes describe inventory/combat beyond this pinned public Unity tree, whose head explicitly says no enemy logic. Hold for reconciliation of publicly present game scope, missing user-supplied data and output target evidence.

title: sp00nznet/macrecomp
reason: Reusable static-recompilation/Toolbox toolkit and dependency rather than a game; record runtime boundary as evidence for Shufflepuck, without adding a separate game row.

title: Rescue Raiders — Apple II partial source reconstruction
reason: Distinct substantive game research root after programmatic catalogue/decision-root screening and primary source/lineage review.

title: Atari 8-bit disassemblies
reason: Repository metadata describes Atari 8-bit disassemblies, but the default branch contents endpoint returns an empty tree and no published artifacts are available to review. Reconsider if source files are restored.

title: Robotron: 2084 — Scott Tunstall arcade reverse engineering
reason: Primary repository documentation and implementation establish commented arcade-game reverse engineering listing within tracker scope.

title: mnaberez/interpod
reason: Primary README, labelled firmware source and ACME recipe establish substantive 6502 peripheral firmware/hardware reverse engineering.

title: PC88Behavior — clean-room NEC PC-8801 replacement ROM
reason: Primary README and implementation evidence establish the independently catalogued scope described by PC88Behavior — clean-room NEC PC-8801 replacement ROM.

title: pappadf/lisa-c
reason: Primary README, Makefile and implementation tree establish a substantial Apple Lisa 68000 cross-development environment with custom object, filesystem, runtime and emulator-test tooling.

title: kz80_chip8 — CHIP-8 to native Z80 recompiler
reason: Translates CHIP-8 opcodes to Z80 ROM plus runtime, with ACIA text rendering of the 64×32 display. Translation direction is CHIP-8→Z80, not Z80→host; shipped game inputs do not prove full compatibility.

title: PAL — restored Commodore assembler sources
reason: Original PAL source made readable/buildable with xa65. Mixed BASIC/assembly and relocatable output are separate flavours, not simultaneous features.

title: tomWangTomWang/PC98-Game-Translator
reason: Generic screenshot translation pipeline rather than PC-98 binary/format restoration. Backend uses local Qwen inference and hardcoded local paths; README references absent requirements files. AI inference is not evidence of AI-authored implementation. Retain only as a lead until a distinct preservation/development role is established.

title: dsk2woz2 — Apple II sector-image conversion
reason: Converts standard 35-track, 16-sector, 256-byte DSK input to WOZ2. Source-level defect: extension loop overwrites has_p and has_dot from the same character, making their conjunction false; documented ProDOS-order detection is not established as working.

title: Fight for Life — restored Jaguar source build
reason: Reconstructs missing pieces around original FFLSRC.ZIP and modernizes build tooling. Retail versus modified/no-trailer outputs are separate; retail identity includes trailer bytes and regenerated security prefix.

title: GeoPatcher — Variable Geo II translation tools
reason: Extracts/edits Shift-JIS text and patches halfwidth display for vanilla VG2 and the Perfect Collection revision. Offsets differ between versions and must be re-extracted.

title: 3it — 3DO graphics conversion and inspection
reason: Image conversion covers CEL/IMAG/LRFORM, palettes and selected NFS containers. No dithering, incomplete CEL option combinations and directional format limits remain. ANIM output and NFS wwww writing are TODOs despite broad introductory wording.

title: 6809 sprite compiler — native generated blitters
reason: Native callable module compiles packed 16-color sprite data into drawing instructions, using color zero as transparency and compact LEAX skip sequences. It trades greater code size for speed.

title: MagSID Xplatform — cross-platform C64 tracker continuation
reason: Avalonia adaptation shares tracker/DAW code, emulated playback and a native SID exporter. Retro sound bank is still incomplete; MP3/FLAC export remains Windows-only while WAV is cross-platform.

title: Z80nDisassembler — Spectrum Next instruction listings
reason: Table/bitfield instruction decoder emits addresses, instruction bytes and mnemonics including indexed forms. It is a listing tool, not a complete interactive code/data recovery framework.

title: SVP development tools — SSP160x assembler and ROM utilities
reason: Implements SSP160x instruction assembly and SVP ROM manipulation alongside research hardware designs. Scope is Virtua Racing cartridge coprocessor, not Mega Drive 68000 instruction assembly.

title: HivePal — Mega Drive palette editor
reason: Palette browsing/editing supports whole ROMs and split data, with binary/assembly-related UI. Data tool, not game decompilation.

title: SN76489 Python — Sega PSG reference core
reason: Sequencer-level PSG core with variant data and clocked write behaviour. Upstream compares attenuation streams with pinned Nuked-PSG, but this is not blanket electrical or analog audio equivalence for every chip.

title: Temple of Apshai — TRS-80 BASIC source archive
reason: Original-style line-numbered dungeon/inn/training BASIC and level files, including1979copyright/revision header. No README does not mean absent source.

title: Out of Gas — Game Boy disassembly
reason: Banked assembly, graphics tables and hardware/memory definitions exist despite minimal README. Many address-derived names remain; no completion percentage inferred.

title: Mappy — Game Gear options-screen translation
reason: Small focused patch replaces the single Japanese options screen with custom drawing code and compressed art. Rest of UI already English; do not inflate into whole-game text recovery.

title: vs-sr-dev/pc-virtualhydlide
reason: Primary repository evidence establishes a distinct in-scope retro-development or software-archaeology project; the matching project audit records CPU, build, runtime and uncertainty boundaries explicitly.

title: mnaberez/vwradio
reason: Primary repository evidence establishes a distinct in-scope retro-development or software-archaeology project; the matching project audit records CPU, build, runtime and uncertainty boundaries explicitly.

title: ruby-Z80 — assembler DSL and Spectrum tooling
reason: Ruby macro-assembler DSL with labels, relocation/debug metadata, TAP output and Spectrum BASIC helpers. Ruby host requirements separate from generated Z80 code.

title: MacResourceFork — template-driven parser
reason: Parses resource forks using TMPL definitions, adding fork-local custom definitions without globally replacing built-ins. Source implements asynchronous template loading.

title: Beehive — Mega Drive content editor
reason: wxWidgets/ion-engine content editor with tiles, stamps and map workflows. Experimental SNES tile support does not establish finished SNES exporters.

title: Captain Tsubasa II — NES translation disassembly
reason: Annotated banked source and symbolic cutscene/nametable routines, with mostly Russian comments. Separate translation-focused repository, not merely a ROM upload.

title: theyoungones2/conk
reason: Amiga game construction kit with Gonk/Bonk/Zonk editors and Ponk runtime plus bundled game projects. Passed to parent for tool-lane handling; one source collection root, not many speculative game records.

title: amigaports/sdl2-amigaos4
reason: Older SDL2 AmigaOS4 repository directs users to AmigaPorts/SDL. Preserve lineage; do not count a second multimedia-library port family.

title: OSCR Jaguar standalone firmware
reason: GitHub identifies this as a downstream fork of Tolbat's reader; the reviewed README carries the same analyzer/16-bit functionality and adds routine build/release automation rather than a distinct preservation project.

title: Cassette 50 C64 CopyCat
reason: Primary README identifies a standalone 2 KiB original 2020 charity-competition memory game; it is source-available homebrew but below the tracker's substantial-homebrew threshold and not an RE project.

title: adventofcode
reason: Advent of Code puzzle solutions, without a historical-computer project or reusable retro-development tool.

title: vitapack
reason: PlayStation Vita VELF-to-VPK packer for small intros; no reviewed historical-platform recovery scope.

title: geolith-libretro
reason: Libretro integration for Neo Geo Geolith emulator; scoped to Neo Geo and no specific contribution to the currently tracked Amiga/Atari/C64/CPC recovery subjects established.

title: DPTSteppedProgressBar
reason: SwiftUI progress-bar widget for current Apple platforms, despite explicit Claude-generated notice.

title: MotionMasks
reason: Generic RLE animation-mask research and bitmap library, with no demonstrated original-software analysis.

title: world-of-warcraft-panic-button
reason: Windows hotkey utility minimizing World of Warcraft windows, unrelated to legacy software recovery or retro development.

title: DayzWillowisps
reason: DayZ creature mod, not historical software work.

title: mailscreener
reason: Modern iCloud mail screening daemon, unrelated to historical software.

title: Chuckulus
reason: Original Acorn Electron/BBC Micro Chuckulus game inspired by Chuckie Egg and Nebulus; distributed disk/tape media alone is not recovery or a reusable tool.

title: jotd666/jungle_king
reason: A 256 KB Z80 listing and post-processing script qualify as an arcade disassembly; repository has no Amiga code, so an Amiga conversion is not claimed.

title: MarkyTurtle/4489_byteloader
reason: GitHub identifies this as a fork of 4489/4489_byteloader; copied README credits upstream and does not establish a separately documented disassembly. The Infinite Dreams README cites this loader in its later single-disk adaptation.

title: MarkyTurtle/HardwareKeyboardReader
reason: README describes new Amiga 500 hardware keyboard library code and an in-progress VS Code example, not a reverse-engineered legacy software subject.

title: CPCtelera
reason: Substantive CPC C/assembly development framework, low-level hardware library, asset tools and reproducible-project build infrastructure. Inspected keyboard implementation directly programs the PPI/PSG; examples and content tools form the same coherent repository.

title: Fruity Frank Kotlin
reason: Substantive Kotlin/LibGDX recreation of Fruity Frank with game-state, enemies, collision, scoring and desktop/Android launchers. It recreates CPC gameplay rather than documenting binary-derived reconstruction. Gradle pins old Kotlin/Android dependencies; no independent build or run was performed.

title: Demonia MSX disassembly
reason: Traced cassette reconstruction with loaders, relocated game blocks and annotated embedded Loriciels monitor. Author supplies tape rebuild and coherence checks; original tape is user-supplied.

title: LibreROM
reason: Early independently authored Macintosh-compatible ROM project. README explicitly limits M1 to a diagnostic reset image; a bootable Macintosh replacement and proposed Amiga/ST hosts are not established.

title: Ms. Pac-Man SNES disassembly
reason: Asar-based SNES disassembly integrated with the author's ROM framework, game-specific RAM/ROM maps and asset extraction scripts. Separate from tracked Amiga and Apple IIgs ports.

title: OpenWINGS
reason: Early behavioural reconstruction of Miika Virpioja's Wings 1.40, not the unrelated Amiga Wings. Ship/terrain source and differential-test harness are present; whole-game completion is not claimed.

title: Star Rider arcade notes
reason: Substantive laserdisc-game research on sprite pages, palette, phrases and memory layouts, with image-bank reconstruction assembly. Not a complete game-code restoration.

title: Zeal 8-bit OS
reason: Portable Z80 assembly OS with kernel, drivers, filesystem, target configurations and SDK examples; native source development rather than binary reconstruction.

title: RoboCop vs. The Terminator audio disassembly
reason: Commented Mark Cooksey engine/data disassembly with WLA-DX integration. Author reports matching audio data, not a playable full game; separate voice sample routine is not covered.

title: Amstrad CPC Toolchain
reason: Linux-hosted CPC development toolchain assembly with vasm/vlink, Exomizer, iDSK, libdsk and graphics converters. Source Makefile inspected; external downloads were not installed or executed.

title: Astron — Palm OS original source
reason: Original author's arcade game source, with game manager, sprite/collision and graphics code. Historical PRC-tools build; non-commercial release conditions, not unrestricted open-source licensing.

title: Next3D — Spectrum Next graphics engine
reason: Documented Z80 rendering library with z88dk C interface, Layer 2 pixel/line/triangle primitives. README marks v0.3 debug mode and not production-ready.

title: Star Control II — 3DO source preservation
reason: Preserved 3DO source/resources and audio support code, distinguished from the later Ur-Quan Masters port. Provenance/release discussion comes from upstream README; build not reproduced.

title: AmigaOS libraries — mixed C reconstruction and binary-preserving corpus
reason: Whole-repository collection includes substantive iffparse C reconstruction and per-library knowledge. Upstream says roughly 1,230 library builds are verbatim hunk-word images, not recovered semantic source. Do not interpret the 1,482-library documentation claim as 1,482 fully understood implementations.

title: Alleyway — Game Boy annotated disassembly
reason: WIP annotated RGBDS source with named ball physics, brick and game-loop routines. README reports roughly 200 named functions and remaining unnamed data; no global completeness or byte-matching inference.

title: Akao — PlayStation sound-driver reconstruction
reason: C driver implementation with PS1 libspu transfer callbacks, instrument and sequencer structures. Early source research; no independently verified matching or runtime completeness.

title: MINIX 2.0.2 — Atari ST adaptation
reason: Later MINIX adaptation includes Atari conditional kernel drivers and enhanced floppy handling. Multi-platform source tree does not mean every target was built or tested.

title: ToeJam & Earl — Mega Drive analysis
reason: REV02-focused code/resource analysis with main-68000 and named Z80 sound driver. Requires supplied ROM; differences from REV00 not fully established.

title: Infocom Apple II ZIP/EZIP/XZIP interpreter disassembly
reason: Partially reversed Z-machine interpreters for multiple historical versions using Macro Assembler AS. Version support is explicit and some revisions remain unsupported; this is interpreter source, not all adventure game data.

title: Apple III Apple II-emulation disk analysis
reason: Partial historical Apple II emulation-disk disassembly for Apple III, including boot/configuration setup and ROM-image layout. System compatibility software, not a game-specific emulation port.

title: Flicky — Mega Drive annotated disassembly
reason: Older independent annotated listing identifies RAM-executed main code and assembler/debugger constraints. Distinct repository from the separately tracked Flicky reconstruction; no matching or completeness measurement performed.

title: rtbinobj — retro object-file converter
reason: GUI/CLI source includes OMF, COFF, Amiga HUNK and BSV writers. README still says DOS-only, while inspected COFF/HUNK modules establish broader implementation; no independent equivalence tests.

title: Snowscape — Archimedes terrain engine
reason: Midwinter-inspired C89/ARM terrain engine; sampled terrain code references original Amiga calculations. An exploratory Archimedes interpretation, not an official Midwinter port or verified full game.

title: Paper Mario decompilation
reason: Structured C code including ambient-audio state machine. Upstream targets US, JP, PAL and iQue images; per-region completion and hash reproduction are not independently measured.

title: Super Mario All-Stars disassembly
reason: Collection-wide annotated bank source. Upstream explicitly warns relocations or code changes may break the ROM and assembly/documentation remain unfinished; no full relocatability claim.

title: Img2CPC image and tile converter
reason: Pixel/tile extraction, palette and mask handling for CPC modes0/1/2 with ASM/C outputs. Source implementation reviewed; palette correctness and target rendering not independently tested.

title: King’s Field reverse-engineering tools
reason: Qt tools for map/database/executable/asset inspection. KF2 is main target; other FromSoftware games largely have model/texture loading only. KF3 names may be wrong or objects absent; editing completeness not implied.

title: MAG MIXER X68000 source
reason: Preserved 16-colour MAG overlay program using selected transparent colours and palettes. Delegates image decoding/display to external viewer; not a standalone MAG codec.

title: FROTH BBC compiler type-in restoration
reason: Corrected rekeying of Jeremy Ruston’s1983 threaded-language compiler. Hybrid FROTH is not full Forth; inline6502 assembly prevents running unchanged under modern BBC BASIC Windows/SDL.

title: RAD DOS preservation reconstruction
reason: Typed segmented C recovered from assembly/Reko with hardware/DOS boundary replacements. Actual functions and register/output modelling inspected; whole-game fidelity and completion not independently demonstrated.

title: TetraPack Amiga unpacker
reason: C implementation of TetraPack unpacking with explicit source register-style state and Hunk support. Historical packer archives are reference inputs; no candidate executable or sample was run.

title: Colleen Calculator source restoration
reason: Carol Shaw source printouts shared with permission, imaged and OCR/proofread, preserving separate 8K and 9K versions. Listing and conversion script are actual source evidence, but finished-version identification remains qualified and no fresh assembly performed.

title: Fusion Forth Atari ST source
reason: 1985 interpreter/compiler/IDE source with threaded execution, Atari trap calls, editor and libraries. Author licence included; historical source is not independently verified to build with a modern assembler.

title: STrinkler Atari executable packer
reason: Atari adaptation of Amiga Shrinkler with PRG/raw modes and verification. Minimal mode trades compatibility for size, larger executables may decrunch slowly; performance claims upstream only and original compression lineage credited.

title: Zero4 Champ PC Engine translation source
reason: Translation source/art/script with specific font and script builders. CSV is the build input; removed ODS spreadsheet is not missing implementation. Requires original game data and compatible WLA-DX/toolchain dependencies.

title: Perihelion Atari ST assembly tutorial republication
reason: Primarily republishes perihelion's existing Atari ST tutorials as AsciiDoc and separates/reformats their assembly examples, with only minor edits. Its short Makefile orchestrates existing vasm, zip2st and Hatari. Reviewed source establishes an educational reference rather than a distinct recovered program or independently implemented development/recovery tool, so retain a source/decision but no separate project.

reason: This is the original programmer's native C++ game conversion, not evidence of a newly discovered assembly decompilation. The inspected game.cpp implements game state directly, and the CMake build links native game, platform and Vulkan sources. Keep all supported outputs under the canonical root and leave reconstruction-method enums empty rather than claiming unproven RE provenance.

reason: Primary Ultima V decompilation with assembly-level semantic matching and playable modern/DOS targets.

title: Le Dernier Serment / The Last Oath — 128 KB CPC adventure
reason: C/SDCC program implements parser, scenes, inventory/database, dialogs and banked graphics/data loading. Windows batch recipe assembles CPC startup routines, compiles Z80 C, converts Intel HEX and assembles a DSK with CPCDiskXP. Original adventure with shared code and separate English/French database and text resources. Classified as subject; native homebrew adventure game. Windows batch compiles C/assembly, converts Intel HEX and makes a DSK using fixed SDCC36 paths, catart, hex2bin and CPCDiskXP. Published game links and a script do not independently establish current compilation/playability; flags remain unknown. Original adventure with shared code and separate English/French database and text resources. MIT covers project code; bundled font, graphics and external tools retain separate provenance and a separate font license is visible.

title: NibblerDX — Amstrad CPC remake
reason: README describes the CPC remake based on Mosaik Software's port, using CPCTelera/SDCC and Arkos Tracker 2. Native C implements snake movement, gems, scoring, rounds and levels. Source plus bootable DSK are present; README calls v0.9 demo fully playable and reports real-hardware testing. Retain demo/version qualification. No independent compile or gameplay validation. The Android export directory is an emulation wrapper and is not a separate native Android reconstruction. Distinct from tracked jotd Amiga arcade transcode. README explicitly says demo v0.9 fully playable, tested on actual CPCs/emulators, and built with CPCTelera 1.5/SDCC. Positive flags remain author claims, not our build/playtest. Android export is an emulator wrapper, not native target. No independent compilation, execution, gameplay, hardware or byte-exact verification was performed. title: DeluxePaint I — original Amiga painting-application source
reason: Archive identifies itself as the original 1986 DeluxePaint/DPaint source, with manuals and reference card. C implementation includes paint-window handling, bitmap/blitter operations, palette tools, IFF I/O and initialization; PRISM.txt preserves the historical overlay/link layout. Computer History Museum license permits individual personal noncommercial use and restricts redistribution, derivative distribution and multi-user hosting; this is source-available archival material, not an open-source release. Historical linker script names amiga.lib, lc.lib and debug.lib. Complete build prerequisites, exact hardware minimum and reproduction of a release binary were not established.

title: Conquest
